name: hcapp_authorizeDevice
description: Device authorization flow. Resolves a user by invite code (URC: prefix via @scanText) or directly by @userId, registers the device in HC.Device, and returns the hasher profile plus a device secret used for all subsequent auth token generation. Returns one of three distinct rowset shapes depending on the outcome — caller must inspect column presence to distinguish error paths from success.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The device UUID. Used as the PK for the new Device record. Expected to be generated once per app install.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Shared access token. Validated via HC.CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 with the null user UUID (00000000-...) — this is a public/pre-auth endpoint.

parameters.name: hcVersion
parameters.description: App version string. Stored on Hasher.HcVersion.
parameters.typeMismatch: Parameter is NVARCHAR(250) but Hasher.HcVersion is NVARCHAR(50). Silent truncation if version string exceeds 50 chars.

parameters.name: scanText
parameters.description: User invite code in 'URC:XXXXXX' format. Used to look up the hasher when @userId is not provided. Mutually exclusive with @userId.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Direct user lookup by ID. When provided, @scanText is ignored for lookup (the user's actual ResetCode is read back into @scanText internally for the error log only).

parameters.name: deviceData
parameters.description: JSON blob of device metadata (OS, browser name, etc.). Stored as-is in Device.DeviceData.

parameters.name: apnsToken
parameters.description: Apple Push Notification Service token. NULL for Android devices.

rowsets.name: AuthTokenError
rowsets.description: Returned only when CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 fails. Non-standard error format — different column names and a non-standard error code (1) from the business error rowsets. No errorId or errorProc column present.

columns.name: ErrorType
columns.description: Always 1. Not in the standard HC errorType table. Pascal-cased unlike the standard rowset.

columns.name: ErrorTitle
columns.description: Always 'Unauthorized Access Token'. Pascal-cased unlike the standard rowset.

columns.name: ErrorDescription
columns.description: User-facing error message. Named 'ErrorDescription' here, not 'errorUserMessage' as in the standard error rowset — non-standard column name.

rowsets.name: BusinessError
rowsets.description: Returned when the user is found but Removed=1, or when no matching user or invite code exists. Uses near-standard error columns but with the wrong errorType code. Caller must distinguish from AuthTokenError by detecting presence/absence of the errorId column.

columns.name: errorId
columns.description: GUID of the HC.ErrorLog entry created for this error.

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: Always 5 ('Unhandled database error') for both business error cases. Should be 3 (auth failure/not found) per HC standards — this is a misuse of the code.

columns.name: errorTitle
columns.description: 'This user has been removed' or 'Invite code not found'.

columns.name: errorUserMessage
columns.description: Full user-facing error message explaining next steps.

columns.name: debugMessage
columns.description: Always 'This is a standard error that is anticipated and does not require debugging'.

rowsets.name: HasherProfile
rowsets.description: Returned on success. Full hasher profile plus device credentials. DeviceSecret and TimeWindow are returned under obfuscated column aliases (iconDataBase64 and colorPaletteIndex) — acknowledged in SP comments as intentional but bad security-through-obscurity.

columns.name: displayName
columns.description: Hasher.DisplayName — persisted computed column (hash name or full name per NameDisplayPreference).

columns.name: qrSecretCode
columns.description: Hasher.QR_secret_code — secret UUID used for QR verification.

columns.name: thirdPartyForceTokenRefresh
columns.description: Hasher.ThirdPartyForceTokenRefresh — signals the app to refresh its OAuth token.

columns.name: iconDataBase64
columns.description: Device.DeviceSecret — deliberately obfuscated alias. This is the cryptographically random 75-char secret used for all subsequent CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 calls. Named 'iconDataBase64' as security-through-obscurity; SP comments acknowledge this as bad practice.

columns.name: colorPaletteIndex
columns.description: Device.TimeWindow — deliberately obfuscated alias. The TOTP-style time window in seconds (30–45, randomly chosen at device registration). Used by the app to generate short-lived auth tokens. Named 'colorPaletteIndex' as security-through-obscurity.

sideEffects: UPDATE HC.Hasher SET LastLoginDateTime = getdate(), HcVersion = @hcVersion, updatedAt = getdate() WHERE id = @userId
DELETE FROM HC.Device WHERE ApnsToken = @apnsToken AND FcmToken = @fcmToken — prior device record cleanup; silently a no-op for Android (see NULL semantics smell)
INSERT INTO HC.Device (id, DeviceSecret, TimeWindow, DeviceData, UserId, ApnsToken, FcmToken)
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on user-removed and user-not-found error paths

codeSmells.issue: Inconsistent error rowset format — three incompatible shapes with no discriminator
codeSmells.detail: The auth token failure returns (ErrorType, ErrorTitle, ErrorDescription) with errorType=1 and no errorId/errorProc. Business errors return (errorId, errorType, errorTitle, errorUserMessage, debugMessage, errorProc) with errorType=5. Success returns the HasherProfile rowset. Caller must infer which path fired by detecting column presence — there is no status flag or consistent envelope.

codeSmells.issue: Wrong errorType for business errors — should be 3, not 5
codeSmells.detail: Both 'user removed' and 'invite code not found' return errorType=5 ('Unhandled database error'). These are fully anticipated business scenarios and should return errorType=3 (auth failure/entity not found). Using errorType=5 misrepresents the failure mode to callers and monitoring.

codeSmells.issue: Device cleanup DELETE silently fails for Android and single-token devices
codeSmells.detail: DELETE FROM HC.Device WHERE ApnsToken = @apnsToken AND FcmToken = @fcmToken uses AND. When either token is NULL (always true for Android, where @apnsToken=NULL), SQL Server NULL-equality semantics mean no rows are matched. Android re-authorizations never clean up prior device records. This is a real data accumulation bug. Should use OR with IS NULL guards, or delete by @deviceId instead.

codeSmells.issue: No transaction — multi-step writes without BEGIN TRANSACTION
codeSmells.detail: UPDATE HC.Hasher, INSERT HC.LaunchAndLogin, DELETE HC.Device, and INSERT HC.Device are all outside a transaction. A failure mid-sequence (e.g. PK violation on Device INSERT if @deviceId already exists) leaves partial state: Hasher updated and login logged, but no Device record created. The app would believe authorization succeeded.

DeviceSecret is aliased as 'iconDataBase64' and TimeWindow as 'colorPaletteIndex'. The SP comment says 'yes I know it's bad'. The values are transmitted as cleartext JSON regardless of alias. HC6 should document these as DeviceSecret and TimeWindow and rely on transport-layer security instead.

codeSmells.issue: @hcVersion type mismatch — NVARCHAR(250) vs Hasher.HcVersion NVARCHAR(50)
codeSmells.detail: The SP parameter is 5× wider than the column. A version string longer than 50 chars would silently truncate on the Hasher UPDATE. Should be aligned to NVARCHAR(50) in HC6.
Any unhandled exception (PK violation on Device INSERT, constraint failure, etc.) surfaces as a raw SQL error to the caller. HC6 must wrap in TRY/CATCH with ROLLBACK.

codeSmells.issue: Device.BuildNumber and Device.Version not populated from parameters
codeSmells.detail: HC.Device has BuildNumber NVARCHAR(25) and Version NVARCHAR(25) columns, both defaulting to '<unknown>'. This SP does not populate them — actual version data is encoded in the @deviceData JSON blob instead. Intentional but undocumented.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
Never rename the obfuscated aliases (iconDataBase64, colorPaletteIndex) without updating the Flutter app's device auth parsing code
